comments.problem: The new `Vmar::protect` contract documents a non-obvious syscall-facing behavior: `protect` can return `Errno::ENOMEM` after already changing pages before the first unmapped hole. That behavior is surprising for a `Result<()>` API and appears to be defined by external `mprotect`/Linux semantics, but the doc comment does not cite the source or rationale. Future readers have to rediscover whether the partial side effect is intentional or an implementation accident.

comments.fix: Do not keep stale mapping starts across calls to `inner.insert_try_merge()`. Remove or drain all affected `VmMapping`s before reinserting any protected ranges, or defer merging until after the loop has processed every pre-collected range. This ensures a later `protect_mappings` entry cannot be removed before its turn.
comments.grounding: Kernel panic reachable from user input
comments.problem: An unprivileged process can build a user-controlled `VMAR` layout that makes this `unwrap()` panic. For example, map three writable anonymous pages, call `mprotect()` on the middle page to make the layout `RW | R | RW`, then call `mprotect()` over all three pages with `PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE`. When the middle mapping is reinserted, `inner.insert_try_merge(taken)` can merge it with the already-writable next mapping and remove that next mapping from `inner.vm_mappings`. The next loop iteration still uses the stale `vm_mapping_range.start`, so `inner.remove(...).unwrap()` can panic in the kernel from user input.

comments.fix: Update `book/src/kernel/linux-compatibility/syscall-flag-coverage/memory-management/README.md` under `### msync` and `book/src/kernel/linux-compatibility/syscall-flag-coverage/memory-management/msync.scml` to document the newly supported `msync` behavior for unmapped pages, including that a range containing unmapped pages returns `ENOMEM`.
comments.problem: This change enhances the user-visible `msync` syscall behavior by recognizing ranges that contain unmapped pages and returning `ENOMEM`, but the Linux Compatibility docs and `msync.scml` are unchanged. The documented syscall coverage can therefore understate or misrepresent the implemented `msync` behavior.
